title: Decision: what MONITOR reports, and why SETNAME is refused
description:
MONITOR and SETNAME are the two IRCv3 verbs of epic mimid-1wgh.140. Bead
mimid-1wgh.140.5 implements them. Seven readings had to be settled, against
~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircv3-monitor.md, ircv3-setname.md,
ircv3-standard-replies.md, ircdocs-modern.html and
ircdocs-modern-numerics.yml for every number, with ~/PROJECT/meshIRCd
(main.go:2442-2541) as the independent implementation.

1. WHAT A 730 MEANS, which is the whole of the bead.

ircv3-monitor.md:21 calls the extension "notification of when clients become
online/offline". MIMI defines no presence at all.

Reading A: answer 730 for a user who is a participant of a room this user
shares. Reading B: answer 730 for a user who has at least one client that is
a leaf of the MLS group of such a room. Reading C: leave MONITOR unanswered,
which is what docs/irc-lessons.md decided before this bead ("no presence in
MIMI; Goguma shows no indicator rather than a wrong one").

CHOSEN: B. A is false: Room.participants comes from the PARTICIPANT_LIST
component and does not move when a leaf comes or goes, so a participant whose
devices were removed -- the state room-policy-04 section 5 leaves a user in,
and the state KICK leaves them in -- would be reported online while receiving
nothing. B is a fact mimid holds and can report truthfully, which is the
epic's class 1 test. C is coherent and was the standing decision; it is given
up because B exists, and because Goguma already sends MONITOR - when it
closes a query (agent-frontends.md:2147), so the verb is being sent at a
client that gets nothing back.

THE COST, stated plainly because nothing in IRC can carry it: a client will
label a 730 "online" and a user will read it as "here". mimid cannot say
whether anyone is at the other end, only whether anything of theirs is in the
group. The crate docs, the numeric's documentation, agent-frontends.md section
7.39 and the crate's # Limitations are the only places that can say so. The
sharp case is the one KICK leaves: a member NAMES still lists, still a
participant, reported offline.

2. WHERE THE FACT LIVES, which widens an IRC bead into the store.

Reading A: a count on the plaintext record (Person.clients), refreshed by the
sync. Reading B: the IRC front end takes the agent lock on the MONITOR path
and asks Agent::clients directly.

CHOSEN: A. B is cheaper to write, takes a lock a sync holds for its whole run,
and has no way to notify on a change, which is most of what MONITOR is for; a
re-evaluation per feed batch under B would take the agent lock on the path
every message takes. A is also not a new kind of crossing: refresh_dids
already projects did and scid from the same leaves onto the same records.
Two asymmetries with refresh_dids are deliberate and documented at the field
and the pass: a user absent from every room is set to 0 rather than left as
the record has it, because a contact who shares no group is unreachable; and
refresh_clients has no second call site on an Event, because Event::MembersChanged
is not journaled for this device's own Commit on its first attempt
(mimid-agent-core agent.rs, `if again`), which is exactly the local KICK. The
moved-epoch gate covers both, every leaf change moving an epoch, and the gate's
record of epochs starting empty so the first sync of each process recounts.

3. ERR_MONLISTFULL: ALL-OR-NOTHING, OR A PARTIAL ADD.

ircv3-monitor.md:148-151: "This numeric is used to indicate to a client that
their monitor list is full, so the command failed. The <limit> parameter is
the maximum number of targets a client may have in their list, the <targets>
parameter is the list of targets, as the client sent them, that cannot be
added."

Reading A: all-or-nothing. A + that would pass the bound adds nothing, and
<targets> is every target it asked to add that is not already in the list.
Reading B: add in order until the bound and put the overflow in 734.
Reading C: meshIRCd's (main.go:2459-2476): insert as you go, and on the first
overflow send one 734 naming that one nick and return, so the nicks added
earlier in the same command get no 730 or 731 at all.

CHOSEN: A, on "so the command failed". B and C both leave the client's idea of
its list and the server's disagreeing about targets neither 730 nor 731 named;
C demonstrably so. A also makes the bound trivially enforceable before any
insertion, so the list can never pass what 005 advertises.

4. A 734 WHOSE <targets> DOES NOT FIT ONE LINE. INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC.

ircv3-monitor.md:146 shows one 734 with one <targets> list and never a
repeated form. A command naming a hundred nicks produces a list the 734 cannot
carry: the incoming line allows about 500 octets of targets and 734's own
overhead leaves about 456.

Reading A: repeat the numeric, one 734 per packed group, each carrying the same
<limit> and description. Reading B: send one 734 with <targets> cut to fit.
Reading C: send one 734 naming only the first target that did not fit
(meshIRCd's shape).

CHOSEN: A, labelled INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC at the code
(mimid-agent-irc monitor.rs, `monlistfull`). B drops names from a diagnostic in
silence. C is not the all-or-nothing reading of point 3 and names a target
arbitrarily. Each line A sends is exactly the spec's shape, so a client that
reads only the first still has a well-formed 734. Tested by
monitor_refuses_a_list_past_its_bound, which asserts both the one-line and the
packed case.

5. A TARGET THAT IS NOT A NICK THIS DAEMON COULD HAVE GIVEN.

ircv3-monitor.md:67-68 says only "For this specification, 'target' MUST be a
valid nick as determined by the IRC daemon", and :38-42 says the extension
"enhances user privacy by disallowing subscription to hostmasks, allowing
users to avoid nick-change stalking". Neither names a reply.

Reading A: refuse the command with FAIL MONITOR INVALID_PARAMS naming the
target; add nothing. Reading B: store it and report it offline, as meshIRCd
does (main.go:2459-2488). Reading C: do not add it, but report it once in 731.

CHOSEN: A. AGENTS.md says to decode strictly and fail closed, and the crate's
own precedent for a malformed parameter is FAIL CHATHISTORY INVALID_PARAMS
(history.rs). B lets junk that can never come online take a slot a real nick
could have had, and is how a nick!user@host target would enter the list at all.
C is the worst of the three: 731 asserts the target is a valid nick that is
offline, and because the entry takes no slot MONITOR L will not echo it, so a
client that re-reads its list re-sends it for ever.

6. A MODIFIER THE SPEC DOES NOT DEFINE, TWO MODIFIERS IN ONE COMMAND, AND A
PARAMETER TOO MANY.

ircv3-monitor.md:48-54 says "The client MUST NOT attempt to specify more than
one modifier. Only one special modifier may be used per MONITOR command", and
:70-101 give each form exactly one target parameter. No reply is named for a
client that does it anyway.

Reading A: FAIL MONITOR INVALID_PARAMS, with the offending token as the
context. Reading B: silence, as meshIRCd gives (its switch has no default).

CHOSEN: A. ircv3-standard-replies.md:46-48 requires an implementer to reuse an
existing registered code, and INVALID_PARAMS is the one this front end already
sends for an unknown subcommand and excess parameters
(ircv3-chathistory.md:141-146, history.rs). B cannot be told from a dropped
line by the client. `MONITOR +-` falls out as an unknown modifier, which is the
same answer. A missing target parameter is 461, and a parameter that was
supplied and holds no target is 461 too, on Modern's USER rule
(ircdocs-modern.html:1213: "If it is empty, the server SHOULD reject the
command with ERR_NEEDMOREPARAMS (even if an empty parameter is provided)");
a bare MONITOR is 461 on Modern's general rule at :1077. MONITOR - answers
nothing for a target that is not in the list and nothing for one that could
never have been, since :81-84 says "No output will be returned for use of
this command".

7. SETNAME: CARRY IT OUT, OR REFUSE IT.

The bead asks for a SETNAME that changes the display name other members see,
or a refusal, and calls a name only this connection reports a lie to the user.

There is no wire effect available. protocol-07's only profile is the
UserProfile/ProfileField structure in an identifierQuery *response* served by a
provider's identity service (draft-ietf-mimi-protocol-07.txt:2644-2672,
endpoint at :2478), never something a client sets; room-policy-04 names
"Nickname" in its terminology alone (draft-ietf-mimi-room-policy-04.txt:209-212)
with no wire field; mimi-content-10 carries no name for a sender. And in mimid
the IRC realname IS the user URI: command.rs sends 352 as "0 <uri>" and the URI
as 311's realname. So a SETNAME asks to change the identity the provider
authenticates.

CHOSEN: refuse, with FAIL SETNAME CANNOT_CHANGE_REALNAME and a description
naming the reason (ircv3-setname.md:84-89, the code for a change rejected "for
any other reason"). INVALID_REALNAME (:79-82) is not used: the refusal is not
about the value sent, which is also why the parameter is not read and a bare
SETNAME is not 461. The `setname` capability is never advertised and no NAMELEN
token with it, which is what makes refusing the command conformant: :28-30 ties
the MUST-support rule to advertising the capability. This declines the one
SHOULD that applies, :32-34's "the server SHOULD handle it silently (with no
response), as historic implementations did", because a user who types /setname
and gets silence cannot tell it from success; the comment at the handler cites
that line and says so. The epic lists SETNAME in class 1; it turns out to be
class 2, there being no mimid fact for it to report.

8. MAX_MONITOR = 100. INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC.

ircv3-monitor.md:60-65 fixes no number and says a MONITOR token with no
parameter means no limit. 100 is ~/PROJECT/meshIRCd's (main.go:2442, `const
monitorLimit = 100`), which AGENTS.md accepts as a source, and is also the
spec's own example token at :65. It is public in 005 and hard to lower later.

Also settled, needing no reading: support is announced by the 005 token alone
and never by a capability (:60-65); TARGMAX gains `MONITOR:` with no limit,
because Modern says a client "SHOULD assume that no commands except the JOIN
and PART commands accept multiple parameters" where TARGMAX is advertised and
the command is not listed (ircdocs-modern.html:5060, example at :5068);
`extended-monitor` must never be advertised, adding only AWAY, ACCOUNT, CHGHOST
and SETNAME notifications for monitored nicks, of which this front end has
none; both FAILs go out with no `standard-replies` capability advertised, as
FAIL METADATA CANNOT_SET already does, since
ircv3-standard-replies.md:49-57 recommends standard replies to a client that
supports the capability and forbids them to no one. Answering MONITOR makes
ISON the deprecated path (:27-28, and ircdocs-modern.html:5263-5265 lists ISON
among the commands "replaced by the IRCv3 Monitor specification"); mimid keeps
ISON and keeps advertising nothing about it.

The code pointers are in mimid-agent-irc monitor.rs, command.rs's `setname`,
register.rs, mimid-agent-store record.rs and sync.rs, and
docs/design/agent-frontends.md section 7.39.
close_reason: Settled from the IRCv3 Monitor, setname and standard-replies specs, the Modern IRC Client Protocol, the MIMI drafts and the code during mimid-1wgh.140.5; monitor.rs, command.rs's setname, register.rs, the Person.clients field, sync::refresh_clients and agent-frontends.md §7.39 carry the pointers.
